title: Mathematical Behavioral Theory
honesty: Equations are derived from published runtime source (continuity/emotional_continuity.py, continuity/relationship.py). Worked numerical traces below are SYNTHETIC demos labeled MOCK — not live agent logs.

sections.title: State vector
katex: I=\text{irritation},\; J=\text{jealousy},\; H=\text{hurt},\; T=\text{trust},\; A=\text{attachment},\; C=\text{confidence},\; X=\text{anxiety}
sections.notes: Auxiliary: apology_credibility Ac, rival_heat map, counters. All continuous dims clamped to [0,1].

sections.title: Bounds
sections.notes: Invariant: every state variable remains in [0,1] after every update.

sections.title: Asymmetric inertia blend (_blend)
sections.notes: ι = inertia ∈ [0,1]. Hostile events accrue more readily; repair is attenuated by high inertia (e.g. albedo jealousy_inertia=0.88).

sections.title: Idle time decay
sections.notes: λ = decay_per_neutral from personality profile. One decay step ≈ 90s idle.

sections.title: Comparison event
sections.notes: s_c=comparison_sensitivity, s_r=rejection_sensitivity, d_T=trust_damage. Then I,J,H updated via _blend with anger/jealousy inertia.

sections.title: Formula 5 — agent relationship update
sections.notes: Neutral=0.50, drift=0.008 per update. Directed edges (A→B need not equal B→A).
